title: Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Make a batter (pancakes) and a dough (chapati or mandazi) with measured ingredients; frying is done by or beside the teacher. Link to Maths: measuring flour and liquid.

skills.key_step: The child identifies batters (runny, more liquid than flour, poured: pancakes) and doughs (stiff, more flour, kneaded and shaped: chapati, mandazi, bread) and matches products to each.

floor.question: How is fat put into flour for scones?

representations: a bowl of batter and a ball of dough

board.do: Draw a spoon of runny mixture and a ball of mixture.

misconceptions.ask: Is chapati made from a batter or a dough?
misconceptions.repair: Show a runny batter poured and a stiff dough rolled.

misconceptions.ask: Which has more liquid than flour?
misconceptions.repair: Measure the liquid and flour for each.

listen_for: A batter, because they are fried
misconceptions.ask: What mixture are mandazi made from?
misconceptions.repair: Show mandazi dough rolled and cut before frying.

misconceptions.ask: Can other flours make flour mixtures?
misconceptions.repair: Show millet pancakes or cassava flour recipes.

checks.question: Is pancake mixture a batter or a dough?
Name a product made from dough.

skills.key_step: The child says how to prepare a batter (measure, sift, beat in eggs and liquid gradually, smooth, rest) and a dough (measure, sift, add liquid a little at a time, knead until smooth and stretchy, rest covered).
steps: Batter: beat in liquid slowly; rest.
Dough: add liquid little by little; knead; rest.

board.do: Write "pour all the water in at once".

misconceptions.ask: How is liquid added to flour for a dough?
misconceptions.repair: Pour all the water into a cup of flour: it turns to sticky paste.
Roll an unkneaded and a kneaded dough.

listen_for: Stir once and leave the lumps
misconceptions.ask: How is a smooth batter made?
misconceptions.repair: Fry a lumpy pancake and a smooth one.

misconceptions.ask: Why are ingredients measured for a batter?
misconceptions.repair: Make two batters, one guessed and one measured, and compare.

checks.question: Why is dough kneaded?
checks.answer: to make it smooth and stretchy

checks.question: Why sift flour for a batter?
checks.answer: to remove lumps and add air

skills.key_step: The child says how products are made: pancakes (thin into a hot greased pan, turn when bubbles burst), chapati (roll, oil, fold, roll thin, cook both sides), mandazi (roll, cut, deep fry by an adult until golden), and tells when each is cooked.

floor.prerequisite: Knows how batters and doughs are prepared.
floor.question: How is liquid added to dough?

representations: a pan and a rolling pin
steps: Heat the pan or oil first.
Chapati: roll thin, cook both sides.

board.do: Draw a pancake with bubbles on top.

misconceptions.ask: When is pancake batter poured into the pan?
misconceptions.repair: Pour batter into a cold pan: it sticks and stays pale.
Watch the bubbles in the demonstration.
Cook a thick and a thin chapati.

misconceptions.ask: Why must oil be hot before frying mandazi?
misconceptions.repair: Recall Grade 5: food in cold oil is soggy.

checks.question: When is a pancake turned?
checks.answer: when bubbles burst and edges set

checks.question: Why roll chapati thin?
checks.answer: it cooks through and stays soft
